rationale: M59 (#825, #861) + the M12.38/#177 deep review. graphql had NO fixture lane at all, so nothing pinned any of the four contracts below, and all four were broken. (1) The symbol range started on the leading `Description`, so `type A` reported line 1 (its docstring) instead of line 2 and `f` reported 3 instead of 4 — measured at 3,131 of 3,332 symbols on the GitHub public schema, 94% of the file's symbols pointing at a line that does not contain the name they are named for. This is the M59/#861 rule (a decorated declaration's line belongs to the name, not to its decorator) with a different decorator, already applied to scala, typescript and javascript. (2) `extend type A { g }` produced NO member at all — 0 of 7 across the corpus sample, and 12 of 12 after the fix. A reader that emitted a symbol for the extension of an already-declared type published a SECOND `class A` with the same identity, which the `forbidSymbols` count below is sized to catch. (3) `implements I1 & I2 & I3` and `union U = M1 | M2 | M3` are LEFT-RECURSIVE rules, so tree-sitter nests them and a direct-children reader keeps only the LAST clause — 496 relationships lost across 47 corpus files, including every multi-interface type in the GitHub public schema. (4) Every relationship carries a `line_number` read off the AST node that NAMES the fact, because the store's relationship identity is (source, target, type, line) and a line-less edge collapses two genuine facts into one row: `f(x: Int): Int` has a return type and an argument type of `Int`, on one line, under two different roles. The `implements` forbids pin the pre-fix line attribution as well as the pre-fix clause loss. `expectSymbolCount` pins the de-duplication half: an `extend` of a type the same file also declares must contribute MEMBERS and NOT a second symbol for the type, because two `class A` rows of one identity is a duplicate in the index. The pre-fix `topLevelDefinitions` read `Definition` straight off `source_file` and found none, which silently disabled the de-duplication for every extension in the file. The symbol LINES are pinned through `expectSymbolRanges`, which is this runner's channel for a symbol's position; `expectSymbols` matches identity (name/kind/ownerName) only, so a line stated there would be a silently unmatched constraint rather than a failing one — measured, and the reason the first version of this fixture failed on every row. Ledger rule R9 applies here too: three declared-type positions in this fixture are `references` + metadata.relationshipType='declared_type', and a `forbidRelationships` row pins the old `uses` label for one of them. The union members (`U -> M1..M4`) stay `uses`: a union member is a NAME in a member list, not a `Type` node in a declaration, which is exactly the line the rule draws.
